answer: For a poll on a marble atlas on a ledge, officials tally yes and no ballots. If the margin is at most 10, they check every voter's ID against the roll, count the first ballot per matching ID and reject mismatches and repeats; otherwise all ballots count. In a close poll, extra passing ballots need more qualifying IDs, potentially costing recruitment effort. Borrowed IDs can pass, and a wide preliminary margin avoids checks.
